cse-2012-cs-45.approach: Track the congestion window transmission by transmission: double in slow start up to the threshold, add 1 MSS per round in congestion avoidance, and on a timeout set threshold = cwnd/2 and restart slow start from the initial window.
cse-2012-cs-45.given:
| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Initial cwnd (slow start) | 2 MSS |
| Initial threshold | 8 MSS |
| Timeout | during transmission 5 |

steps.title: Slow start up to the threshold
steps.body: Transmission 1 uses $2$ MSS, transmission 2 uses $2\times2=4$, transmission 3 uses $4\times2=8$ = threshold, so slow start ends here.

steps.title: Congestion avoidance, then timeout
steps.body:
Above the threshold the window grows linearly: transmission 4 uses $8+1=9$, transmission 5 uses $9+1=10$. The timeout during transmission 5 sets
$$\text{threshold}=\frac{10}{2}=5\text{ MSS},\qquad \text{cwnd}=2\text{ MSS}.$$

steps.title: Slow start again (capped at 5)
steps.body: Transmission 6 uses $2$, transmission 7 uses $2\times2=4$, transmission 8 would double to $8$ but is capped at the threshold $5$.

steps.title: Linear growth to transmission 10
steps.body: Transmission 9 uses $5+1=6$ and transmission 10 uses $6+1=7$ MSS. So the window at the tenth transmission is $7$ MSS.

optionAnalysis.reason: 8 MSS is the window if slow start were not capped at the new threshold, or one ACK-round beyond the tenth transmission.
14 MSS would need the old threshold (8) to survive the timeout and keep growing; a timeout halves it.
Correct: 2, 4, 8, 9, 10 (timeout, threshold 5), 2, 4, 5, 6, 7.
12 MSS ignores the timeout entirely (8, 9, 10, 11, 12 …).

pitfalls: Forgetting that the threshold becomes half of the window at the moment of timeout (10/2 = 5), not half of the old threshold.
Doubling past the threshold in the second slow-start phase (4 → 8 instead of 4 → 5).
